description: Kitora's application shell: a thin composition of @kitora/sidebar with a header (breadcrumbs, search, notifications, user menu), page header with tabs, a resizable inspector on the dock's SplitView, a status bar, a mobile drawer, and layout presets (sidebar, double sidebar, top nav, settings).

exports.name: SHELL_LAYOUTS
exports.description:
The layout presets:
- `sidebar`: one sidebar beside the content (Linear, Vercel).
- `double`: an app or workspace rail outside the sidebar (Slack, Discord, VS Code).
- `top-nav`: no sidebar on desktops, the nav runs across the header (GitHub, Stripe docs).
The settings preset is `SettingsLayout`, a section nav inside the content of any of these.

exports.name: buildTocTree
exports.description:
Nests `headings` by level. The shallowest level present is depth 0, so a page whose top headings are `h2`s does not render an empty `h1` tier;
a skipped level (an `h4` straight under an `h2`) nests one step, not two. `maxDepth` drops deeper headings (default: keep all).

exports.description:

exports.name: BOTTOM_NAV_HEIGHT_PX

exports.name: nextBottomNavScroll
exports.description:
The bar's next state for one scroll step: shown while focused, at the top and at the end; hidden once the page has moved down by more
than `threshold` since the anchor, shown again once it has moved up by more than it; otherwise unchanged (and the anchor kept, so
slow scrolling still adds up).
exports.signature: ({ hidden, anchor, top, maxTop, focused, threshold }: BottomNavScrollInput) => BottomNavScrollState

exports.name: BottomNavScrollInput
exports.description: One scroll step's facts, the input of {@link nextBottomNavScroll}.

exports.name: collectHeadings
exports.description:
The headings under `container` matching `selector`, in document order. A heading without an id is given one from its text (deduplicated with a
`-2`, `-3` suffix) so its link has a target; pass `assignIds: false` to skip those headings instead. Headings marked `data-toc-ignore` are skipped.
The label is the heading's `data-toc-label` when set (a shorter name for the list), else its text.
exports.signature: (container: ParentNode, selector?: string, assignIds?: boolean) => { readonly headings: TocHeading[]; readonly elements: HTMLElement[]; }

exports.name: observeHeadings
exports.description:
Observes `elements` and reports every heading's position (`above`, `in` or `below` the reading band) whenever one changes. Returns the stop
function. Where IntersectionObserver is missing (an old engine, a test DOM), it reports nothing and the list simply shows no active entry.
exports.signature: (elements: readonly HTMLElement[], onChange: (positions: ReadonlyMap<string, TocHeadingPosition>) => void, options?: HeadingSpyOptions) => () => void

exports.name: prefersReducedMotion
exports.description: Whether the reader asked for less motion; a smooth scroll becomes a jump then.

exports.name: scrollToHeading
exports.description:
Scrolls `id`'s heading to the top of its scroll area (smoothly unless the reader prefers reduced motion) and moves focus to it without a second
scroll, as following an in-page link does, so the next Tab continues from the section. A heading that is not focusable gets `tabindex="-1"`.
Given `root` (the scrolling box the headings live in), only that box scrolls: the page around it stays where it is. Without one the heading
is scrolled into view, which moves every scrolling ancestor, the window included. Returns false when there is no such element.
exports.signature: (doc: Document, id: string, smooth?: boolean, root?: Element | null) => boolean

exports.name: scrollToHeading
